text: Sports will prepare our youths to be physically and mentally prepared for the challenges of the real world and my biggest concern is actually the unvaccinated young children below 12 years old.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: At the moment, physical education lessons for Primary schools are very controlled or suspended.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: In fact, most national school sports meet and games have also been halted for almost two years now.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: This stoppage of physical activities has an unhealthy and negative effect on young children and youths.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Not only are they not able to exercise, they are not able to interact with their friends and are also unable to develop their physical and mental strengths through sports and games.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: It is important for MOE to take a risk-based approach to gradually open up sports activities and CCAs in Primary schools and restart the national school sports meet and games in the Secondary schools and Junior Colleges.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Poh Li San, you have half a minute left.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: As the pandemic situation wanes, sports that are played in the outdoors, such as track and field, and those with minimal contact and played indoors, such as table tennis and badminton, should restart.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Hopefully, team sports with less contact like volleyball and netball can also restart.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Understandably, contact sports like soccer and rugby will take some time but the game could be reorganised into smaller teams so that children can resume playing again in a safe manner.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Singapore is still very much a young nation and our sporting culture is still evolving.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: Sports can be a viable professional career in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: What is important is that we search, focus, nurture and persevere to build a solid and strong foundation for our sporting ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I believe that I speak for all Members of this House when I say that we are extremely proud of all our athletes who represented and continue to represent Singapore, be it at the Olympics, Paralympics or any other sporting event.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We have seen for ourselves how sports have the capacity to rally a nation and inspire generations.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Sports, therefore, play a crucial and important role in forging a strong Singapore spirit.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Sportsmen and sportswomen also serve as good role models for our youths, with their passion, perseverance, drive and values in sportsmanship.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Athletes like Yip Pin Xiu and Joseph Schooling are good examples.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: But as we celebrate and recognise the successes of our athletes, we should also cast our minds towards the equally important task of improving the support system for all our committed elite athletes who are striving hard every day in their respective sporting disciplines regardless of the eventual outcomes in competitions.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: If we succeed in establishing a strong, multifaceted support system for our athletes, a strong national sporting culture can evolve where our athletes can train and aspire to be the best that they can be, while having the peace of mind that they have the financial support during and institutional support after their sporting careers.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: In order to achieve this, the Government can consider working further with the private sector by creating an official platform and invite like-minded private sector organisations to come on board to spearhead these efforts.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: At the moment, we do have various existing programmes by the Government and the private sector in support of the sporting community.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Working closely with the private sector, we will be able to access a wider range of resources and utilise these resources flexibly to benefit a wider spectrum of athletes in more sporting disciplines.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We will also be able to better tailor the support given to each athlete as requirements may differ from athlete to athlete and from sport to sport.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Separately, a perennial worry for elite athletes is their livelihoods after their sporting careers are over.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: The spexBusiness network has done well in this area for many of our athletes but such a committee can look to leveraging the existing network to do even more.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: While we may not be able to adopt a similar model, the committee can look at other innovative arrangements, suited to our local context, for our Singapore athletes.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: My sincere hope is that successes such as those of Pin Xiu and Joseph and the many athletes that have come before them, can inspire a whole new generation of Singaporean athletes to pursue their sporting aspirations.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We, as Members of this House and the Government, must certainly try our very best to support this endeavour.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: My heartiest congratulations once again to all our Olympic and Paralympic athletes for their best efforts in representing Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We are all so very proud of you.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And even as we celebrate the successes today, I thank them for their vision and suggestions in looking forward, looking ahead on what else we can do.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As usual, Ms Phua has also set me a task – and also, thank you for acknowledging my alternative career as a sports commentator.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I will take on board the suggestions and, of course, be accountable to the various initiatives that she has set out.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I have no doubt she will ask me to explain the dashboard to her, in her words, on a different occasion.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And finally, I thank Mr Sitoh for his suggestions.
